bookingPages.title: Booking pages
bookingPages.intro: A public page where clients pick a time themselves. You decide which meeting types are on offer and when you are free — bookings land in your calendar, automatically or after you approve them.

features.title: Draft vs live
features.body: The badge at the top of the builder says whether the page is up. "Publish" saves it and takes it live in one press; while it is a draft the link works for nobody. To take it down, switch off "Publish page" in settings and save.

features.title: Meeting types
features.body: Choose which types the visitor sees, and give each one its own length here — that length belongs to this page alone and never changes the type on another page. With none chosen, the page offers a single meeting at the default length.

features.title: Weekly availability
features.body: Add one or more time ranges to each day. The five numbers above set how often a start time is offered, how long a meeting runs, how much time is kept clear after it, how far ahead someone must book, and how far into the future booking is open — each has a "?" beside it.

features.title: Google Calendar
features.body: With the calendar connected under "Connections", every approved booking is written to it as an event, and the client can be invited too if they left an email. Without a connection the switch is off — the bookings are still kept here.

tips: A time range has to be at least as long as the meeting — a half-hour window against a 50-minute meeting produces no times at all, and the app stops you before publishing.
"Needs approval" holds the time while you decide, so the same slot cannot be taken twice in the meantime.
A short link in settings makes the address memorable — worth setting one before you send it to clients.

faq.q: Does the client need an account?
faq.a: No. The page is fully public, and the client leaves a name and contact details as they book.

faq.q: Why does the calendar look empty to a client?
faq.a: Usually one of three: the page is still a draft, there are no time ranges on the coming days, or the minimum notice blocks them.

faq.q: How is this different from a lead page?
faq.a: A lead page collects an enquiry for you to answer; a booking page takes a slot in your calendar right away.

community.title: Community
community.intro: One shared room for everyone using Simplicity. Before your first message you pick a display name — that is what members see beside you.

features.title: The room
features.body: Every message in one room, oldest to newest. A new message appears for everyone straight away, with no refresh.

features.title: Display name
features.body: The name shown beside each of your messages. A first name, a nickname or your business name — whatever you are comfortable showing. You can change it later.

features.title: Deleting a message
features.body: You can delete your own messages, and only those. Deletion is final — there is no undo, and a sent message cannot be edited.

features.title: Reserved names
features.body: Names associated with Simplicity or its support team are blocked so nobody can impersonate us. Official accounts carry a verified mark.

tips: Your display name is public within the community. If you would rather not be identified by your full name, use a nickname.

faq.q: Who can see my messages?
faq.a: Everyone with an active Simplicity account. It is one shared room, not a private chat.

faq.q: Can I edit a message after sending?
faq.a: No. You can only delete it.

faq.q: Can I add a profile photo?
faq.a: Not yet. For now it is a display name only.

sitePages.title: Public pages
sitePages.intro: One system for building public pages: landing pages, lead-capture pages and booking pages. Build from sections by dragging, design freely, and publish under your own link.

features.title: Section-based building
features.body: Add sections from the palette (hero, text, image, benefits, testimonial, button, form), drag to reorder, and click a section to edit it in the side panel. The center preview is exactly what visitors see.

features.title: Flexible design
features.body: In the 'Page design' panel choose a font, brand color, background (nature photo / color / your own upload), card opacity and blur, and alignment. You can upload images and pick icons.

features.title: Desktop and mobile
features.body: A toggle at the top of the editor switches between desktop and mobile preview, so you can check the page looks good on both.

features.title: Form and booking
features.body: A form section collects details straight into your leads — with manual or automatic approval and a thank-you message. A button can link to an external site, scroll to the form, or lead to booking.

tips: Publish the page (the 'Publish' toggle in the editor) to get a public link — a draft page isn't reachable.
Set a short slug in the 'Public address' field for an easy link to share.

faq.q: Does the visitor need to log in?
faq.a: No. The pages are fully public. Only you see the submissions that come in.

faq.q: What's the difference between the three kinds?
faq.a: Landing page — a full marketing page; Lead page — a form-focused page; Booking — pick a time from your calendar. All on the same design engine.

home.title: Home
home.intro: Home is your personal dashboard. It's made up of widgets you can turn on, turn off, and rearrange however you like. Each one gives you a quick look at a different area of your work and a shortcut to get there.

features.title: The cards that make up the screen
features.body: The screen is built from cards: Daily quote, Overview, How are you today, Quick add, Things needing attention, Tasks and reminders, and Quick numbers. The full list — and everything you can switch on, off or reorder — is in "Settings → Look and display → Home screen", or by pressing and holding a card here on the home screen.

features.title: Overview widget
features.body: A circle that shows whether you're on pace: how much of your daily goal you've already hit. 100% means you're exactly on track. Below the circle you'll also see "X% of goal" — how much of your overall goal you've completed. Tapping the circle expands it with a summary sentence, a progress bar for each active goal, and a "Full details" link to the Overview screen. If you haven't set any goals yet, a "Set a goal" prompt will appear that takes you straight to the Goals screen.

features.title: Daily quote widget
features.body: One inspirational quote per day. Tapping it opens the Quotes panel, where you choose the source — "System quotes" or "My quotes" — and can add or delete your own. As long as you haven't added any personal quotes, a quote from the general library is shown.

features.title: Daily check-in widget
features.body: Shows the next unanswered daily question. Answer on a 1–10 scale (drag the slider and save with ✓) or with yes/no, depending on the question. After answering, you move to the next question; when you're done, "You're done for today — great" appears. If you've turned on a daily reminder and its time has passed, a gentle nudge appears: "You haven't answered today — take a moment for yourself?" You can dismiss it, and tapping the question takes you to the Daily Check-In screen.

features.title: Quick transaction / quick update widget
features.body: Two buttons: "Quick add" opens shortcuts to add a transaction, client, lead, task, project, goal, reminder, or session — all right from Home. "Update goal" lets you pick a goal category and manually log progress.

features.title: Things needing attention card
features.body: A card that collects everything waiting for you in one place: transactions to confirm, sessions you haven't marked yet, clients with an outstanding balance, a gap from the monthly goal, urgent tasks, clients you haven't spoken to in 45 days, leads with no activity, follow-ups due today, and duplicates against Google Calendar. Transactions open a window where each row has "Yes, it happened", "No, it didn't" and delete; sessions open a confirmation window (confirm / skip / delete); everything else takes you to the relevant screen.

features.title: Confirming sessions from Home
features.body: In the "Sessions to confirm" window inside the alerts card, you can mark each session as "Took place" (which creates a real session in the client or group card), "Did not take place", or delete it. You can also confirm, decline, or delete an expense linked to that session.

features.title: Tasks and reminders card
features.body: One card bringing together your open tasks and your upcoming reminders, by urgency and date. The summary shows how many are urgent out of the total, a red dot marks an urgent task, and tapping a row opens the matching screen. The ✓ marks it done — a repeating reminder simply jumps to its next date, and you can take it back with "Undo".

features.title: Quick numbers card
features.body: Three cards — Tasks · Net · Clients — each with a live number on top. Tapping one opens a filter and detail window (by time, type, status, urgency, project, category, group) with a trend chart, and the number updates to match your filter. "Open in full" takes you to the full screen. Net counts only confirmed transactions, and the card title switches to "Income" or "Expenses" if you filter to a single type.

features.title: First-time welcome card
features.body: Until you have at least one client, a "Everything starts here" card sits at the top of the screen with three steps — first client, first task, and first lead — each linking to the screen with the add button highlighted. You can hide it with X, and it disappears on its own once your first client is created.

features.title: Adjusting the display, and sending feedback
features.body: In "Settings → Look and display → Appearance" you can change the card style (Glass or Solid), the letter thickness (Regular or Thick) and the spacing between items (Tight, Regular or Roomy) — with a sample card that changes in real time. At the bottom of the home screen there is a "Got feedback?" card for suggestions and bugs.

tips: Want to redesign Home? "Settings → Look and display → Appearance" for the card style, letter thickness and spacing; "Home screen" for choosing what appears and in what order.

You set the order by pressing and holding a card here on the home screen and dragging it, or with the arrows in "Settings → Look and display → Home screen". The quote and overview cards always sit in the top row when they are on.
Tapping the Tasks / Net / Clients card doesn't just show a number — it opens a full filter, and your settings are saved for next time.
"Quick add" on Home is a shortcut to add anything in the app (transaction, client, lead, task, project, goal, reminder, session) without switching screens.
Marked a reminder or task by accident? You can undo it immediately using the "Cancel" notification that pops up after the action.
Marking a session as "Took place" in the session confirmation window creates a real session in the client card — it doesn't just clear the alert.

faq.q: How do I add or remove a card from Home?
faq.a: "Settings → Look and display → Home screen" — there is a switch for every card. You can also do it right here: press and hold a card to enter edit mode, then ✕ hides it.

faq.q: What does the percentage in the Overview circle mean?
faq.a: It's how much of your daily goal you've hit so far — not a grade. 100% means you're exactly on pace. Tapping the circle shows a breakdown for each goal.

faq.q: I tapped the "Clients" / "Net" / "Tasks" card and got a filter window — where's the full screen?
faq.a: The cards open a detail and filter window. To get to the full screen, tap "Open in full" at the bottom of the window.

faq.q: Why doesn't the "Net" number on the quick numbers card match what I entered?
faq.a: The card counts only confirmed transactions (not ones awaiting approval, and not ones you marked as "Didn't happen") and shows net for the time range you selected in the filter window (default: this month). Transactions awaiting approval appear separately under "Needs attention".

faq.q: I marked a recurring reminder as done — did it disappear?
faq.a: No. A recurring reminder isn't deleted — it just jumps to its next date. If that was a mistake, tap "Cancel" in the notification that pops up to bring it back.

faq.q: How do I change the daily quote or add my own?
faq.a: Tap the quote widget to open the Quotes panel. There you choose the source — "System quotes" or "My quotes" — and add or delete your own.

clients.title: Clients
clients.intro: This is where you manage all your clients. Each client has a card with their sessions, payments, and status. You can group, sort, and perform actions on multiple clients at once.

features.title: Adding a client
features.body: The "+ New client" button opens a short form: name, phone and status. Only the name is required — everything else can wait. Below them, "Billing, meetings and more" expands to the rest: billing mode (package / per session), number of sessions and price per session, meeting type, sub-status, project, email, address, date of birth and a recurring meeting (day + time). No field was removed — it just stays out of the way, and you can fill it in later from the client's file.

features.title: Client statuses
features.body: Every client belongs to one of four groups: Active, Paused, Former, No status. The tabs at the top of the list show the groups with a count for each. The "No status" tab only appears if there are clients in it. In Settings you can add your own sub-statuses to each group, and they'll appear in the status picker in the client form.

features.title: The "View" button — sorting, grouping and selecting
features.body: The three controls that change the shape of the list sit together in one menu. Sorting orders by name, balance, paid, sessions, date added or longest-standing, ascending or descending. Grouping switches between status and project. "Select multiple" turns on selection mode. Each choice is saved for you and comes back next time you open the screen.

features.title: Grouping by status or project
features.body: At the top of the "View" menu is a status / project toggle. In project mode clients are listed under each project name (including "No project"), and the tabs and the summary above disappear — which is why the button itself changes to "View · Project", so it is clear where they went.

features.title: Search and the open-balance filter
features.body: The search bar matches on the client's name. The "Open balance" button shows only those who still owe, and the number beside it counts everyone who owes — across all statuses, not just the open tab. The filter itself crosses statuses too: with it on you will also see paused and former clients who still owe, so no debt hides in a tab you rarely open.

features.title: Top summary (monthly / cumulative)
features.body: Above the list (when grouping by status) a summary of the open group is shown: sessions, paid, and open balance. The "Monthly / Cumulative" toggle determines whether the sessions and amounts are for the current month or from the beginning. In the "Former" and "No status" tabs the summary is always cumulative and the toggle is locked.

features.title: The client file
features.body: Tapping a client opens a side panel: the billing summary (sessions / paid / balance), quick actions, and sections that expand — weekly recurring meeting, sessions & summaries, payments, payment plan, open tasks, timeline, more details, notes, linked reminders and group memberships. The pencil beside a section heading does one of two things: on the recurring meeting, more details and notes it opens a small form in place, with Save and Cancel; on the sections that are lists (sessions, payments, tasks, timeline, reminders) it makes the rows tappable, and tapping one opens it for editing.

features.title: Quick actions in the file
features.body: Four buttons at the top of the file: "Log session" for a meeting that already happened (date, summary, private notes), "Schedule meeting" for a future one — either one-off or a weekly recurring slot, "Got paid" to record income, and a WhatsApp button that opens a chat with the client. Below the billing summary there is also "Adjustment", which opens the three figures above it — sessions, paid and balance — for editing.

features.title: Changing the status from the file
features.body: The status label in the file is a button — tap it and pick another group, with one-step Undo. A client who belongs to a group takes the status from that group and is marked "· by group", but you can still pick a status by hand and your choice wins over the group. It is then marked "Manual", with "Back to group status" beside it to clear the override.

features.title: Editing details and billing
features.body: The "Edit" button opens the full form in sections: details, meetings & scheduling, billing & payments — and groups, which only appears for a client who is in one. That is where you find the billing mode, personal sessions ("scheduled" and "held"), price per session, a "Total due" that overrides the automatic calculation, and the "Paid" and "Balance" fields you can type into. Changing either of those last two opens the Adjustment sheet, so even a manual correction carries a reason and a date. Notes, address and birth date are not in this form — you edit those on the card itself, through the pencil beside "More details" and "Notes", so that every field has exactly one place it is edited.

features.title: Adjustments — a discount, an import fix, cash that was never booked
features.body: The "Adjustment" button below the billing summary opens the card's own numbers exactly as they read — "Scheduled" and "Held", "Paid" and "Balance" — only now you can correct them. Everything updates as you type: raising "Paid" drops "Balance" straight away, and changing the session counts re-bills the client. Each money figure that moves gets its own question: "Paid" can be an "Imported data fix" or a "Payment received, never recorded", while lowering "Balance" is always recorded as a discount — an amount forgiven without claiming anyone paid. Changing both at once saves in one go and files two rows, because each is a different reason. A line appears for everything that will change before you save, and you can add a note ("cash at the session"). Sessions are not money: they are written straight to the client with no reason, and a hand-edited "Held" is stored as the gap against what the app actually logged. Every money adjustment appears as a dated row under Payments, so the total above always adds up to what is listed beneath it; written-off debt sits in its own group, since it is not part of "Total paid". An adjustment never reaches your finance reports; if the money really did arrive, use "Record as income instead". The pencil beside "Payments" gives every adjustment row a delete button, and removing one puts the amount back where it was moved from.

features.title: Selecting several clients at once
features.body: "View" → "Select multiple" turns on selection mode: tick a few clients and the bar that appears at the bottom offers "Change status", to move them all to another group, or "Delete". Both are reversible with a single Undo.

features.title: Deleting a client and handling transactions
features.body: Deleting (from the card or the selection toolbar) opens a choice window: "Keep transactions" leaves the payments in Finance with a "[Name] · deleted" label, or "Delete transactions too" sends them to the Trash as well. Every item can be restored from the Trash within 30 days.

features.title: Sessions and groups in balance calculation
features.body: Individual sessions count toward the calculation, and in "per session" mode the balance accumulates based on the number of logged sessions × the price. A client who is a member of a group also sees that group's sessions and charges, which are counted in the summary accordingly.

tips: Sorting, grouping, the monthly/cumulative toggle, and the "Open balance" filter are all saved per user — whatever you chose will be restored next time you open the screen.
Moving a few clients to "Former" at the end of a season? "View" → "Select multiple" → tick them → "Change status" in the bar at the bottom.
To keep things precise, add sub-statuses in Settings (e.g. "Short break", "Waiting for confirmation") — they'll appear in the status picker in the client form.

Imported data and the numbers do not line up? "Total due" in the edit form straightens the overall figure, and to correct "Paid" or "Balance" use "Adjustment" with the reason "Imported data fix" — that way there is a record of why the number moved.
A client placed in a group takes its status from that group and is marked "· by group". You can override it by hand — it will be marked "Manual", and one tap returns it to the group's status.

To set a weekly recurring meeting: open the file → "Schedule meeting" → recurring slot. The day follows the date you picked. To change or clear it later, the short way is the pencil beside "Weekly recurring meeting" inside the file.

faq.q: Searching by phone or email doesn't find the client — why?
faq.a: Search only works by client name. To find someone by other details, sort or browse the list and open the card to see the phone number and email.

faq.q: Is my clients’ information protected?
faq.a: Yes. Each account reaches only its own data, and no other user of the system can reach your clients. The team has limited technical access for operation, support and backup only.

faq.q: I deleted a client by accident — can I restore them?
faq.a: Yes. Right after deletion an undo option appears, and in any case the client is kept in the Trash for 30 days. Note: if you chose "Delete transactions too", restoring the client alone does not bring back the transactions that were deleted with them — choose "Keep transactions" if preserving payment history matters to you.

faq.q: I changed "Paid" in the client's details but nothing was recorded in Finance?
faq.a: Changing "Paid" or "Balance" opens the Adjustment sheet, where you say what happened. An adjustment updates the client's file only and never appears in your finance reports — that is deliberate, for discounts and import fixes. If the money genuinely arrived, pick "Payment received, never recorded" and then "Record as income instead", and a real payment is created in Finance.

faq.q: Why does the top summary show zero sessions or ₪0 this month?
faq.a: When the toggle is set to "Monthly", the summary only counts sessions and payments for the current month. Switch to "Cumulative" to see everything from the beginning. In the "Former" and "No status" tabs the view is always cumulative.

faq.q: What's the difference between "Package" and "Per session" billing?
faq.a: With "Package", the balance is calculated based on the number of scheduled sessions × the price per session. With "Per session" there's no fixed quantity upfront — the balance accumulates based on the number of sessions you've actually logged × the price per session.

faq.q: What is the "Unitemised adjustment" row?
faq.a: It appears when the adjustments on a client add up to more than the listed rows explain — for example one made from the mobile app, or one recorded before this screen could store reasons. Rather than leave an unexplained gap, the difference is shown as its own row, so the total above always matches what is listed beneath it.

leads.title: Leads
leads.intro: A board for managing all your inquiries. Track every lead from the moment it's "In progress" until it becomes a client — with sources, labels, and follow-ups.

features.title: Two views: Leads and Statuses
features.body: Two tabs sit at the top of the screen. "Leads" shows the kanban board. "Statuses" opens a panel for managing labels without leaving the screen. Your selection is saved, and the screen opens in the same view next time.

features.title: Kanban board with three columns
features.body: Leads are organized in three fixed columns: In progress, Converted, Not relevant. Each column shows how many leads are in it, and tapping a card opens the "Edit lead" window.

features.title: Dragging between columns
features.body: You can drag a lead card from one column to another, by touch or with a mouse. If the target is off-screen, hold near the edge and the board scrolls by itself until that column arrives. If the column you dragged to has two or more labels, you'll be asked which one — "Which stage?" in "In process", "Which reason?" in "Not relevant" — and you can always skip. If there's only one, it's selected automatically. Dragging to "Converted" asks nothing. Right after the move, "Undo" appears to go back to the previous status.

features.title: Adding a lead
features.body: Tap "+ New Lead" to add an inquiry. Fill in name (required), phone, source, project, group (only shown when the project has groups), stage (when you've set up stages for "In progress"), inquiry date, follow-up date, and notes. A new lead always goes into the "In progress" column.

features.title: Editing a lead
features.body: The edit window updates every detail and moves the lead between columns via the status buttons. Below them sits the field for the current column: "Stage" in "In process", "Reason" in "Not relevant". Changing the status clears that choice, and changing the project clears the group. Leaving without saving asks first.

features.title: Converting to a client
features.body: A lead that hasn't become a client yet has a "Convert to client" button at the bottom of its card. A window opens with the name and phone already filled in. You can pick a project and a group — a lead that closed gets no label; the project is what describes it. On save a new client is created (active, with no sessions or price yet), the notes carry over, and the lead moves to the "Converted" column with a link to the client. If you picked a group, the client is added to it as a member.

features.title: Lead sources
features.body: Every lead can be tagged with a source — referral, Instagram, website, etc. In the add and edit windows you can create a new source on the spot without leaving: choose "+ New source…", type a name, and it's saved and selected immediately. A card without a source is labeled "No source".

features.title: Labels: stages and reasons
features.body: In the "Statuses" view you can add, delete, and reorder (by dragging) the labels inside each column — stages in "In process" (e.g. "Waiting for a callback"), reasons in "Not relevant" (e.g. "Too expensive"). Clicking the coloured dot on a chip opens a colour picker. The label appears as a coloured dot on the lead card and drives filters and charts. "Converted" has no labels — a lead that closed is given a project. A default label can't be deleted; when you delete another one, leads are left with no label.

features.title: Search, filter and sort
features.body: A search box and a "Filter" button sit above the board. Search matches name, phone, email, notes, source or project, and is not case-sensitive. "Filter" opens a sheet with period, project, group, label, source and date sorting — the number on the button counts the active filters (sorting isn't counted, since it hides nothing). Your selections are saved.

features.title: Follow-ups
features.body: When you fill in the "Follow-up" field on a lead, a reminder is set. The "Follow-ups due today" strip at the top of the screen counts leads it's time to get back to (that are still in progress). Tapping it opens "Open follow-ups" — a list where you can open a lead or mark the follow-up as done (which clears the date). An overdue follow-up is highlighted in red on the card.

features.title: This month's stats
features.body: Three numbers sit at the top of the screen: "Inquiries this month", "Converted to clients", and a percentage labelled "of this month's enquiries". All are calculated automatically from the leads opened this month.

features.title: Buttons on the card: convert, WhatsApp and delete
features.body: The actions sit on the card itself, with no menu. The ✕ in the top corner deletes — a confirmation window with the lead's name opens first, and only then does the lead go to the Trash, where it can be restored within 30 days. Along the bottom row: "Convert to client" (only on a lead that hasn't converted yet) and a WhatsApp button. Clicking the card itself opens the editor.

tips: Fill in a "Follow-up" date so the lead shows up in the follow-ups strip on the day you need to get back to it. That way no inquiry slips through.
Tag each lead with the right source. The conversion rate and other stats rely on this to show you where your best-fit clients are coming from.

Instead of opening the edit window, just drag a card to another column to advance a lead. If the column you want is off-screen, hold near the edge and the board scrolls itself. Made a mistake? Tap "Undo" that appears right after the drag.

Set up your own stages for "In process" in the "Statuses" view (e.g. "Waiting for a callback", "Intro call scheduled") and your own reasons for "Not relevant", then filter by them on the board to stay focused.
When converting to a client you can already assign them to a project and group. Notes from the lead transfer automatically to the new client card.

faq.q: How do I add or color a lead source?
faq.a: You can create a new source directly from the add or edit lead window using "+ New source…" (it gets a default color). For full name and color management, tap "Lead sources" in the screen toolbar — it opens a dedicated panel to add, color and delete sources.

faq.q: A lead I converted to a client still shows on the board — is that normal?
faq.a: Yes. Converted leads move to the "Converted" column and stay there, labeled "Converted to client" with a link to the client. You can filter by project to focus your view.

faq.q: I dragged a lead to another column and was asked which label — why?
faq.a: When the column you dragged to has two or more labels, the app asks which one to assign — "Which stage?" in "In process", "Which reason?" in "Not relevant" — and you can always skip. If there's only one, it's selected automatically. If there are none, the lead moves without one. Dragging to "Converted" doesn't ask at all.

faq.q: I deleted a lead by accident — can I restore it?
faq.a: Yes. The lead goes to the Trash and can be restored within 30 days. The same goes for a deleted label or source — "Undo" appears for immediate restoration, and they can also be restored from the Trash.

faq.q: Does converting to a client set a price or number of sessions?
faq.a: No. The conversion creates an active client with only the name, phone, and notes. The number of sessions and price start at zero and are filled in from the client card.

faq.q: Why does the percentage at the top show a dash (—) or look off to me?
faq.a: It is calculated from the leads opened this month — how many of them are now in the "Converted" column, which is why the label reads "of this month's enquiries". If there are no new inquiries this month, "—" is shown. And a lead moved back out of "Converted" is no longer counted.

finance.title: Finance
finance.intro: The Finance screen is your central hub for all business income and expenses, month by month: transactions, recurring templates, categories, summaries and profit, and invoice imports from your external service.

features.title: New Transaction (Income / Expense)
features.body: The "+ New Transaction" button opens a window where you choose "+ Income" or "− Expense" and fill in the amount, date, description, and client/project. For expenses, you can select a category (or create a new one on the spot). The transaction is saved to the month of the date you chose.

features.title: Future Date Saves as "Awaiting Approval"
features.body: A transaction with a future date is automatically saved as "Awaiting approval" until that day arrives, and sits in the card of transactions awaiting approval. A transaction dated today or in the past is saved as "Confirmed" and goes straight into the summary.

features.title: Issue a Receipt on Save
features.body: For income linked to a client that isn't future-dated, a "Issue receipt on save" checkbox appears (only if you've connected a valid invoicing service). Check it, choose a document type (tax invoice receipt / receipt / tax invoice), and for receipt-type documents also choose a payment method — the document is issued the moment the transaction is saved.

features.title: Monthly Summary and Month Navigation
features.body: At the top of the screen you'll see "Net This Month", "Income", and "Expenses" for the selected month, with arrows to go to the previous or next month. Each number also shows the percentage change from the previous month. The summary counts only confirmed transactions — ones awaiting approval, ones marked "Didn't happen", or ones cancelled by a credit note are not included.

features.title: Cumulative Income Chart
features.body: A chart showing how approved income accumulated day by day over the selected month, with a dot on the current day. If you've set a monthly income goal in the Goals screen, a dashed target line and achievement percentage are shown. If not, a link to set a monthly income goal appears instead.

features.title: Transactions Awaiting Approval and Bulk Approval
features.body: All of the month's transactions awaiting approval sit in a separate card, showing the total income and expenses waiting. Each row has "Yes, it happened" and "No, it didn't". Clicking a row opens editing, and above a list of more than one there's an "Approve all" button — it first opens a confirmation dialog stating how many transactions are involved and the income and expense totals.

features.title: Transaction List: Confirmed and Didn't Happen
features.body: Below the awaiting-approval card, transactions are grouped into "Confirmed" and "Didn't happen". A transaction you marked as not having happened gets a "Didn't happen" tag with a strikethrough amount, and you can move it back to awaiting approval. When there are such transactions, a button appears to show or hide them ("Show N that didn't happen" / "Hide what didn't happen").

features.title: Deleting a Transaction from the List or Edit View
features.body: Every transaction — confirmed, or marked "Didn't happen" — has a delete button in the list, and the edit window also has a "Delete" button. Both open a confirmation dialog naming the transaction's description and amount first, and the delete only happens once you confirm. Right after deletion, an undo notification pops up so you can restore the transaction.

features.title: Recurring Templates (Standing Orders)
features.body: In the "Recurring Templates" section you set up transactions that repeat automatically: "By schedule" (monthly on a specific day, or weekly on a specific day of the week, with an optional end date) or "After a session" (creates a transaction awaiting approval for every session with the client you choose, and closes automatically if the session is skipped). The system generates transactions from these that wait for your approval. Deleting a transaction the rule created also pauses the rule — otherwise it would recreate it immediately; the dialog says so first. If only that one occurrence is wrong, "No, it didn’t" takes it off the pending list and the rule carries on next month.

features.title: Pausing, Editing, and Deleting a Template
features.body: Each template has a pause/resume button — a paused template doesn't generate new transactions and is marked "Paused". You can edit a template or delete it (with confirmation). Transactions already generated from it remain even after deletion.

features.title: Expense Categories
features.body: In the "Expense Categories" section you manage your expense categories: type a name, choose a color, and click "Add". Deleting a category (with confirmation) doesn't delete the expenses — they simply remain without a category.

features.title: Income by Project / Expenses by Category
features.body: Two cards show a column breakdown: "Income by Project" splits approved income across projects (income with no project goes into "No Project"), and "Expenses by Category" splits approved expenses by category ("No Category" for anything untagged).

features.title: Invoices You Issued in Your Invoicing Service
features.body: If you've connected Green Invoice or SUMIT, invoices you've issued in the external service appear in the "Invoices you issued in your invoicing service" section. Each invoice has a "View" link to the document, and you can import it as income or dismiss it. Importing opens a confirmation dialog showing the amount and the client name before anything is recorded. If there's already an income entry for the same client and amount, a "Possibly a duplicate" label appears and that same dialog is worded as a stronger warning.

features.title: Issuing an Invoice and Credit Note from the Edit View
features.body: Clicking on an income entry opens editing, and there — if you've connected an invoicing service — "Issue Invoice" appears: choose a document type, a product from the provider's catalog or free text, and a payment method (for receipt-type documents). After issuing, you'll see the document number and a view link, and a "Credit / Cancel" button that issues a credit note — this cancels the document and removes the income from summaries (the transaction is marked "Cancelled by credit note").

features.title: CSV Export
features.body: The "Export CSV" button at the top of the screen downloads a file with all transactions in the currently displayed month (date, type, amount, description, status, client, project, and category). The button is active only when there's at least one transaction in the month.

tips: All numbers on the screen — the summary, chart, and breakdowns — are for the month shown at the top. If a transaction seems missing, check that you're on the right month based on its date.

Only "Confirmed" transactions count toward the summary and chart. Transactions awaiting approval appear separately until you approve them, and ones marked "Didn't happen" or cancelled by a credit note are excluded from the totals.
For fixed expenses like rent, subscriptions, or supplies — set up a recurring template so the transaction is created automatically each month and you never forget to log it.
You can create a new expense category directly from the transaction window ("+ New category...") without leaving it.
Deleting a transaction opens a confirmation dialog with its description and amount first; once it's gone, the undo notification lets you restore it right away.

faq.q: I logged a transaction but it doesn't show in the list or summary?
faq.a: First check that you're on the right month (based on the transaction's date). A transaction with a future date is saved as "Awaiting approval" and sits separately in the awaiting-approval card until you approve it — only a confirmed transaction counts toward the summary.

faq.q: Why doesn't the summary at the top match what I expect?
faq.a: The summary counts only "Confirmed" transactions. Transactions awaiting approval, ones you marked "Didn't happen", or ones cancelled by a credit note — none of them are counted in the net, income, or expenses totals.

faq.q: How do I set up a standing order?
faq.a: In the "Recurring Templates" section, click "+ New Template", choose "By schedule" (monthly or weekly) or "After a session", and set the amount, day, and end date. The system will generate transactions awaiting approval based on your settings, which you then approve.

faq.q: I deleted a recurring template — what happens to transactions already generated from it?
faq.a: They remain. Deleting a template only stops future transactions from being created; every transaction already generated stays as normal. If you just want to pause it temporarily, use the pause button instead of deleting.

faq.q: Where do I download the data to Excel?
faq.a: Use the "Export CSV" button at the top of the Finance screen — it downloads all transactions from the currently displayed month. To export a different month, navigate to it with the arrows and then click the button.

faq.q: I deleted a transaction by mistake — can I get it back?
faq.a: Yes. Deleting opens a confirmation dialog naming the description and amount first, and right after the deletion an undo notification pops up so you can restore the transaction. You can also undo a "Didn't happen" mark and move the transaction back to awaiting approval.

projects.title: Projects
projects.intro: The Projects screen organizes your work by area. Each project groups clients, groups, tasks, and transactions together, and shows how many clients it has, how much revenue it brings in, and how many open tasks it has.

features.title: New Project
features.body: Click "+ New Project" (or "Add Project" when the screen is empty) to open the "New Project" window. All you define is a project name and a color from a palette of eight. There are no date, budget, or description fields.

features.title: Project card
features.body: Each project appears as a card with a colour dot, a name and three numbers: how many clients, how much revenue (in the range you picked) and how many open tasks. Next to the name is a tag: it shows the group count if the project has groups, "Finished" if the project is done, and "Active" otherwise. Tapping the card opens the full project screen.

features.title: Monthly or Cumulative
features.body: At the top of the screen there's a "Monthly" / "Cumulative" toggle that changes the revenue range. In "Monthly" mode the numbers show the current month's income. In "Cumulative" mode they show all income from the beginning to today.

features.title: Search and sort the list
features.body: From six projects upwards, a search box and a sort menu appear above the list. Search is by project name, is case-insensitive, and every word you add narrows further. You can sort by "Newest" (the default), "By name", "Highest income" or "Most clients". If the search finds nothing, a message appears with a button to clear it.

features.title: Projects Summary
features.body: The "Projects Summary" card at the top of the screen shows how many projects exist, how many clients are assigned to them, and total revenue ("Monthly Income" or "Cumulative Income", depending on the toggle).

features.title: Automatic Revenue by Project
features.body: The revenue on each card is calculated automatically from income transactions linked to the project — or linked to a client who belongs to the project. You don't need to enter amounts manually on the project itself. The open task count also comes from tasks belonging to the project or its clients.

features.title: Editing and deleting from the card
features.body: Every card has a pencil button ("Edit project") that opens the "Edit project" dialog for the name, colour and status, and a bin button ("Delete project"). Deleting asks for confirmation and reminds you that the clients and transactions stay — they just lose the project link. You can also delete from inside the project itself: the pencil at the top of the screen opens the same dialog, and "Delete project" sits at the bottom of it.

features.title: Project status: active or finished
features.body: Every project has a status — "Active" or "Finished" — set in the "Edit project" dialog. A project marked finished leaves the active list and its card gets a "Finished" tag. Nothing else moves: its clients, groups, tasks and transactions stay exactly as they are, and the "Projects summary" at the top of the screen keeps counting it — money that came in really came in, and closing a project does not change that. Note this differs from a group's status: finishing a project does not change any client's status.

features.title: Active or all
features.body: As soon as one project is finished, an "Active" / "All" switch appears above the list (with the number of finished projects beside it). "Active" is the default. If every project is finished, the list says so and offers a button to show them. This switch only hides and shows cards — it does not change the numbers in "Projects summary".

features.title: Project screen: header, people and money
features.body: The top of a project shows its name with the colour dot, and beneath it how many active clients it has (and any "paused" ones). Below that are two cards: the first counts clients and groups, the second shows the money — income, expenses and net. The arrow returns to the projects list and the pencil opens "Edit project".

features.title: Income, expenses and net
features.body: The money card shows three figures: what the project brought in, what it cost, and what is left. Both sides are counted exactly the same way — transactions tagged to the project, or transactions of clients belonging to it — otherwise the difference between them would mean nothing. A "Monthly" / "To date" switch in the card's corner moves all three together between the current month and everything since the start. A net below zero is coloured.

features.title: Project overview ring
features.body: If you have linked goals to this project, a ring with a percentage appears at the top of the screen — how well you are keeping the pace those goals need by the end of the period, with how much of the goal is already achieved below it. Tapping the ring opens a per-goal breakdown with two bars each: pace and achievement. If the project has no goals yet, a "Set a goal for this project" button appears in the ring's place and opens the goal form with the project already filled in. Progress updates are made on the Goals screen.

features.title: Quick add inside a project
features.body: Every project screen has a "Quick add" button that opens a picker: transaction, client, task, goal, reminder or meeting. Whatever you choose opens with the current project already filled into its project field — but you can change it in the form, and whatever you leave there is what gets saved. (A meeting is linked to a client rather than a project, so it has no project field.)

features.title: Income-through-the-month chart
features.body: Below the add row there's an "Income through the month" chart showing how the project's income accumulated over the month, with the total beside the heading. If there's no income this month, "No income for this project this month." is shown. Note this chart always covers the current month — it does not follow the monthly/to-date switch on the stats card above it.

features.title: Groups in a Project
features.body: In the "Groups" section you can create a new group ("+ New Group") with a name, color, pricing ("Package price", "Per-session price", or "No fixed price"), and optional day, start time, end time, and start/end dates. Each group displays the number of members, pricing, recurring session, a members list, and buttons to "Add Member", "Log Session", view past sessions, and delete. You can also edit a group via the pencil button in its header, and remove an individual member by clicking the X on their tag.

features.title: Past Sessions for a Group
features.body: The calendar button on a group card opens the "Past Sessions" list, where each session is numbered automatically. You can change a session's date directly in the list, or delete an individual session — deletion asks for confirmation and removes the session from all group members.

features.title: Group Status and Its Effect on Clients
features.body: Each group has three status buttons: Active, In Development, Ended. Switching to "Active" or "Ended" may also move group members to the appropriate client status (Active / Former) — the system asks for confirmation and shows how many clients will be affected. Switching to "In Development" doesn't change client statuses.

features.title: Assigning a Client to a Group by Dragging
features.body: In the "Clients" section you can drag a client onto a group card. If the client already belongs to another group, a "Assign to Group" window opens letting you choose between "Move here" and "Add (both)". If the client isn't in another group, they're added directly.

features.title: Project Clients
features.body: The "Clients" section shows all clients in the project, with their group tag or a "Private" tag if they're not in a group. Clicking a client opens their client card, and "+ Add Client to Project" adds a new client who is pre-linked to the project.

features.title: Upcoming meetings
features.body: The "Upcoming meetings" section gathers the project's future meetings — those of its groups and of its clients. Each row shows the name, the date and time, and a tag saying how many days away it is. The section is open by default, and tapping a row opens the calendar. Up to six meetings are listed; if there are more, the count is stated with a link to the calendar. A confirmed or skipped meeting is no longer upcoming and does not appear here.

features.title: Project tasks
features.body: The "Tasks" section gathers the project's tasks — both the ones you tagged to it directly and tasks belonging to its clients (in which case the client's name appears under the task title). The number beside "Tasks" is how many are still open; hovering it shows the full picture ("2 of 5 tasks still open"). Each task has a ✓ to mark it done (tapping again reopens it) and a bin to delete it, and an undo message appears right after a delete. "Add task" opens a new task already linked to the project.

features.title: Linked reminders
features.body: The "Linked reminders" section gathers the reminders tied to the project. The number beside the heading is how many are still active; hovering it shows how many out of how many. You can mark a reminder done, delete it (with confirmation) or add a new one for the project. A reminder past its time is marked "Overdue", a completed one "Done", and one coming up soon gets a tag saying how many days away it is.

features.title: Project leads
features.body: The "Leads" section shows the leads assigned to the project, each with its classification. Tapping a lead opens it directly in its edit card on the Leads screen, and "+ Lead for this project" opens a new lead already tied to the project. Leads that arrived from a lead page and are still awaiting approval do not appear here — they sit in the approvals section of the Leads screen.

features.title: Project lead pages
features.body: The "Lead pages" section shows the public lead pages assigned to the project, each with a "Live" or "Draft" tag. Tapping a page opens it straight in the editor. If no pages are assigned, there is a link to create one. The pages themselves are built and managed on the Pages screen.

tips: For income and clients to appear in a project — link transactions, clients, and sessions to it. Revenue is also calculated from transactions belonging to linked clients, not just transactions tagged directly to the project.

Toggle between "Monthly" and "Cumulative" on the main screen to see either this month's income or all-time income. Note that inside the project screen, the "Income This Month" stat always shows the current month.
Deleted a project by mistake? An undo notification appears right after deletion, and either way the clients and transactions remain in the system.
When a project ends, mark it "Finished" rather than deleting it. It leaves the list but all its history stays, and its income keeps counting in the summary and the reports.
Add clients, transactions, and reminders via "Quick Add" inside the project — everything will automatically be linked to the current project, no manual selection needed.
Before changing a group's status to "Ended", be aware that it may move all group members to "Former" status. The system will ask for confirmation and show how many clients will be affected.

faq.q: How do I set a budget, start/end dates, or description for a project?
faq.a: You can't — a project only has a name and a color. There are no budget, date, or description fields for projects. Financial tracking comes automatically from linked transactions. (Start and end dates exist only for groups within a project, not for the project itself.)

faq.q: How do I filter projects by status (active/finished)?
faq.a: Open "Edit project" (the pencil on the card, or at the top of the project screen) and choose "Active" or "Finished". As soon as one project is finished, an "Active" / "All" switch appears above the list — "Active" is the default and "All" brings the finished ones back. The filter touches the list only: "Projects summary" keeps counting every project, so revenue that already came in does not vanish from the report. Note this differs from a group's status (active / in development / ended), which does affect the group members' status.

faq.q: The revenue in a project doesn't look right — why?
faq.a: Revenue sums income transactions linked to the project or to a client in the project, within the range you've selected (monthly or cumulative on the main screen, current month inside the project screen). Transactions not linked to the project or one of its clients won't be included.

faq.q: What happens to clients and transactions when a project is deleted?
faq.a: They stay in the system — they just lose their project assignment. An undo notification also appears right after deletion.

faq.q: I deleted a group — what happens to its members, sessions, and reminders?
faq.a: When you delete a group, a window opens where you choose, for each type of linked data (members, upcoming sessions, past sessions, linked reminders), whether to keep or delete it. Members who are kept remain as private clients in the project. If the group has no linked data, it's simply deleted. You can cancel the entire action with one click.

faq.q: How do I add a group session?
faq.a: Inside the project screen, on the group card, click "Log Session". The session is logged for all group members and numbered automatically. You can see the list of past sessions via the calendar button on the card, and from there edit a session's date or delete an individual session.

tasks.title: Tasks
tasks.intro: One screen for everything still open. "Tasks" are things to do — with a due date or without one. "Reminders" are tied to a day and time and can repeat. "All" shows both in a single list ordered by urgency, and that's what opens when you arrive.

features.title: Three views: All, Tasks, Reminders
features.body: At the top of the summary card is a toggle with three buttons. "All" is the default, because it answers "what's open right now" without making you pick a half to look at first. "Tasks" and "Reminders" are where you organise one kind in depth. Switching views resets the filter to "Open", and the add button follows the view — in "All" it adds a task.

features.title: How the "All" list is ordered
features.body: The list splits into six groups, top to bottom: Overdue, Today, Urgent, This week, Later, No date. A deadline that has passed or lands today beats everything. Right behind it come the tasks you flagged "Urgent" — including the ones with no date at all — so they don't sink to the bottom underneath reminders that aren't due for weeks. A group with nothing in it isn't shown.

features.title: What decides the order inside a group
features.body: The top three groups read by the clock: "Overdue" leads with the oldest debt, and "Today" is a day plan. In the groups below them priority leads and the date only breaks the tie, because nothing down there is on fire. A reminder is read as "Normal" — it carries no priority of its own, and it never enters the "Urgent" group.

features.title: The "View" menu
features.body: The button beside the tabs holds everything that changes the list: grouping, filtering by category, multi-select, and editing your statuses and categories. Whatever is active shows on the button itself even when the menu is shut, so a filter never hides. In "All" you can group by urgency (the default), date or priority; in "Tasks" by priority, project or category; reminders are always grouped by date.

features.title: Adding a task
features.body: Tap "+ New task", fill in "What needs doing?" (required) and pick a priority: Urgent, Normal or Low. You can add a due date and time or leave it out — both are fine. Under "More details" you can link it to a project and a client, write an explanation, and if you've set up statuses or categories, choose those too.

features.title: Priority and the coloured dots
features.body: Three levels: Urgent, Normal and Low. The dot at the end of each row always shows the group that row sits in, so the group heading is its legend. When you aren't grouping by priority, an urgent task says so in words instead — an "Urgent" chip on the row itself.

features.title: Completing a task and undoing it
features.body: Tapping the circle marks it done, and tapping again brings it back. An undo toast appears after every tap, in case you hit the wrong one. Marking done clears any custom open status; reopening doesn't restore it — you can pick it again from the edit sheet.

features.title: Editing, quick rename and deleting
features.body: The pencil on a row opens the edit sheet, with the same fields as the add sheet and a delete button at the bottom. To change just the title, double-tap it and edit in place without opening anything. Everything you delete goes to the Trash and can be restored for up to 30 days.

features.title: Postponing to tomorrow
features.body: A row whose time has come or gone gets a calendar icon that pushes it to tomorrow at the same hour. The push is measured from today, not from the old date — so even something three weeks late really moves to tomorrow instead of staying overdue. There's an undo toast.

features.title: Search
features.body: The magnifier opens a search field that looks through the title, the details, and the name of the linked client or project. Closing the field clears the query, so a filter is never left running behind a shut icon.

features.title: Multi-select
features.body: Through "View" then "Select multiple", the circle on each row becomes a checkbox. You can pick tasks and reminders together and then mark them done, assign a category or delete them — all at once, from an action bar that floats above the list. Changing a filter or searching clears the selection, so you can't delete rows you can no longer see.

features.title: Filtering by status
features.body: Above the list are two tabs: "Open" and "Done". Reminders get a third, "Recurring", which shows the standing schedule — grouped by weekday, monthly, and every-so-many-days. The "Done" list is ordered from the most recent thing you finished downwards.

features.title: Statuses and categories
features.body: Through "View" then "Statuses & categories" you add and remove your own statuses and categories, each with a name and a colour. Every status belongs to either "Open" or "Done", so the counts on the home screen stay right. Deleting asks for confirmation and doesn't delete the tasks themselves — they simply lose that label. The same categories are the filter pills in that menu, and several can be active at once.

features.title: Clearing what's done
features.body: The "Done" tab has a "Delete completed" button that deletes everything the list is showing in one go — with a category filter active, only what's inside it. It all goes to the Trash and can be restored for up to 30 days.

features.title: Adding a reminder
features.body: In the reminders view tap "+ New reminder", fill in "What should we remind you about?", choose how often it repeats (one-off / weekly / monthly / every X days) and set the timing. A recurring reminder can take an end date, be linked to a client, and carry extra details.

features.title: The timing fields follow the repeat
features.body: First you choose how often the reminder repeats, and then the matching timing field appears. One-off asks for a date and time. Weekly asks for a day of the week and a time. Monthly asks for a day of the month (1–31) and a time. Every X days asks for a start date, a time and a number of days.

features.title: Completing and advancing reminders
features.body: A one-off reminder you tick moves to "Done". A recurring one is never marked done — it jumps to its next slot on its own ("Reminder advanced") and keeps jumping until the next slot falls after the end date you set. There's an undo toast here too.

features.title: The summary card
features.body: Above the list is a summary card with three numbers: open, a number that changes with the view — "Urgent" in Tasks, "Overdue" in Reminders and in "All" — and done. All three are counted inside the active category filter, so the card always describes the same list sitting below it.

tips: A task can have a due date or not — both are fine. What makes a reminder different is that it always has a time, and it can repeat.
A task flagged "Urgent" with no date doesn't sink to the bottom: in "All" it gets a group of its own, right after "Today".
Link a task to a client to tie it to them — search will then find it by their name too. Meetings with a date belong in the calendar, not here.
Set up statuses and categories once through "View", and you can filter by category from that same menu — several categories can be active together.
A recurring reminder doesn't disappear when you tick it — it jumps to its next slot. If several slots have piled up unhandled, an ×N chip appears beside the title in the "Open" tab.
Tapped by mistake? An undo toast appears right after every tap on the circle and puts it back.

faq.q: Where do I set a due date for a task?
faq.a: The "New task" sheet (and the edit sheet) has a "+ Add a due date" switch that opens a "Due date" field and a time. A date on its own is enough — the time defaults to 09:00 — and removing the field clears the deadline. A task with no date is perfectly fine; in "All" it appears under "No date", unless you flagged it "Urgent".

faq.q: Why does an urgent task sit above a reminder that's due sooner?
faq.a: Because the list is ordered by urgency, not by date alone. A deadline that has passed or lands today still beats everything, but past that point a task you flagged "Urgent" rises above future work — even when the reminder is due sooner. If you'd rather have a pure timeline, switch "View" to group by "Date".

faq.q: Why does a task I set for today show as "Overdue"?
faq.a: When you set a date without a time, the app fills in 09:00 — and from that hour on the deadline counts as passed. If it matters that the task stays under "Today", give it a later time in the time field beside the date.

faq.q: How do I delete a single task?
faq.a: Open it with the pencil and use the delete button at the bottom of the sheet. To delete several at once there's "View" then "Select multiple". Everything goes to the Trash and can be restored for up to 30 days.

faq.q: I ticked a recurring reminder — why didn't it move to "Done"?
faq.a: That's how it's meant to work. A recurring reminder jumps to its next slot on its own rather than being marked done, so that it keeps coming back. It stops only when the next slot falls after the end date you set.

faq.q: I deleted a status or a category — what happens to the tasks that used it?
faq.a: The tasks stay. They simply lose that label and appear with no status or category. The status or category itself can be restored right away from the undo toast.

faq.q: What's the difference between "Urgent" and "Overdue" in the summary?
faq.a: It's the same slot in the summary card, changing with the view. In Tasks it counts open tasks at priority "Urgent". In Reminders and in "All" it counts whatever is past its time and still open.

calendar.title: Calendar
calendar.intro: The Calendar brings everything you have planned into one place — sessions, reminders, tasks, financial transactions, lead follow-ups, and events synced from Google. You can view it four ways: Board, Day, Week, and Month.

features.title: Four views
features.body: At the top of the screen there are four tabs. "Board" is a list of upcoming events. "Day" shows a detailed hourly timeline. "Week" shows seven columns, one per day. "Month" is a monthly calendar with color dots. Your chosen view is saved and will open again next time.

features.title: Navigating between dates
features.body: In "Day" view, use the arrows to move one day forward or back, with the date shown in the middle. In "Week" and "Month" views, the arrows jump a full month, and there is a month and year picker in the middle. The "Today" button brings you back to today's date (in Week and Month it also jumps to the Day view). In "Board" view there is no date navigation — it always shows events from today onward.

features.title: Adding via "+ New Event"
features.body: The "+ New Event" button opens a window called "New Event" with four options: "Client Session", "Reminder", "Task", and "Transaction" (income or expense). Each choice opens the appropriate add form.

features.title: Scheduling a client session
features.body: In the "Schedule Session" window, choose a client, date, and time. Clicking "Save" creates a session that is pending confirmation. Sessions added here are one-time only. For a recurring weekly slot, set it from within the client card edit, not here.

features.title: Clicking an event — details and actions
features.body: Clicking an event opens "Event Details". For a pending session you will be asked "Did this session take place?" — "Yes" confirms it and "No" skips it. For a session already confirmed, you will see "Session confirmed." next to "Delete meeting" — a two-tap delete that removes both the meeting from the calendar and the session it created on the client card, with an immediate undo. For a reminder you can "Mark as done" or "Delete" (deletion requires two clicks — you need to confirm "Sure? Delete"). For a lead follow-up you can click "Follow-up done".

features.title: Google Calendar events
features.body: Events from Google are marked with a "Calendar" tag and appear alongside your other events. In the details window you can click "Edit" (title, start time, and end time) or "Delete" (two clicks — "Sure? Delete"). The change only affects Simplicity, not your Google Calendar itself. An event you have edited is labeled "Your event (edited in Simplicity)", and your changes are preserved through future syncs.

features.title: View filter
features.body: The filter button at the top of the screen opens "View Filter". There you choose which event types to show: "Sessions", "Reminders", "Lead Follow-ups", and "Google Calendar Events". When you have hidden a type, the button is highlighted so you know the filter is active.

features.title: Duplicates with Google
features.body: Sometimes a recurring session in the app conflicts with a Google event for the same client or group — on the same day, within an hour and a half of each other. In that case a banner appears: "1 calendar duplicate with Google" (or "N calendar duplicates with Google"). Clicking it opens "Calendar Duplicates", where for each pair you choose what to hide — the app session or the Google event — by clicking "Hide".

features.title: Lead follow-ups and reminders
features.body: An active lead with a follow-up date appears in the calendar at 09:00 on that day (without a tag). Clicking "Follow-up done" clears the follow-up date and removes the event from the calendar, but the lead itself stays in its column. Reminders — both one-time and recurring — appear with a "Reminder" tag.

features.title: Connecting Google Calendar
features.body: In Connections > Google Calendar, choose from which date to sync (up to one year back) and click "Connect Google Calendar". You can then click "Sync now", assign each event to a client, project, lead, or group via "+ Assign to…" (each event is marked "Identified" or "Unidentified"), or click "Disconnect".

tips: In "Board" view you only see events from today onward. If the list is long, click "Load more" to see additional events.

"Day" view shows hours from 06:00 to 22:00 on a timeline. Events outside that range do not disappear — they appear in "Before 06:00" and "After 22:00" strips above and below the timeline, and all-day events appear in the "All day" strip at the top.
In "Month" view each dot is colored by type: sessions, reminders, and calendar events (see the legend below the calendar). Clicking a day automatically jumps to its Day view.

A weekly recurring slot you set in the client card is automatically spread out as sessions in the calendar. Each time the calendar opens it fills in any missing sessions in the background, rolling forward.

If you chose to hide a Google event to resolve a duplicate, it may come back on the next sync because the sync is one-directional. It is usually better to hide the app session instead. (Editing or deleting a Google event from "Event Details" does persist through future syncs.)

faq.q: How many views does the calendar have?
faq.a: Four: "Board" (list of upcoming events), "Day" (hourly timeline), "Week" (seven columns), and "Month" (calendar with dots). Switch between them using the tabs at the top of the screen — your choice is saved for next time.

faq.q: I clicked "+ New Event" — why is there no name or duration field?
faq.a: "+ New Event" first asks what you want to add: a client session, reminder, task, or transaction. A session is set by client, date, and time — there is no free-text name field or duration here.

faq.q: Does scheduling a session in the calendar automatically record it as income in Finance?
faq.a: No. Scheduling a session here only creates a session pending confirmation, and confirming it ("Yes") only marks it as having taken place. Recording income is done separately — it does not happen automatically when you schedule a session.

faq.q: How do I set a recurring weekly session?
faq.a: Sessions added via the calendar are one-time only. To set a recurring weekly slot, edit the client card and set it there — the calendar then spreads it out automatically into future sessions.

faq.q: I edited or deleted a Google event in the calendar — does that change it in Google too?
faq.a: No. Editing or deleting a synced event from "Event Details" only affects Simplicity, but those changes do persist through future syncs (the event becomes "your event"). Only hiding a Google event to resolve a duplicate might revert on the next sync.

faq.q: Why is a certain event not showing in the calendar?
faq.a: Check "View Filter" — you may have turned off that event type (sessions, reminders, lead follow-ups, or Google Calendar events). Google events only appear after you have connected and synced in the Connections screen.

goals.title: Goals
goals.intro: Here you set measurable goals for your practice. Progress is tracked automatically from data already in the system, or entered manually. Each goal has a card showing how much has been achieved and whether you are on pace.

features.title: New goal
features.body: Clicking "+ New Goal" opens a window where you choose a metric, give the goal a name (optional), set a time frame, a numeric target, and an importance level. You can also link it to a project and group. Each goal appears on the screen under the category of the metric you chose.

features.title: Choosing a metric
features.body: Some metrics are tracked automatically — "Revenue", "Active Clients", "Leads", "Closings", and "Group Members" — and there is also "Other — Manual Updates" for tracking you manage yourself. You do not need to set up categories separately: the category is created automatically from the metric you choose.

features.title: Time frame
features.body: Choose between "Monthly", "Weekly", or "By Date". "Monthly" is measured over a full calendar month, "Weekly" over the current week. With "By Date" you add a target date, and progress is measured from the day you created the goal up to that date.

features.title: Automatic tracking
features.body: "Revenue" goals sum income transactions in the period. "Leads" and "Closings" are counted from your leads (leads by inquiry date, closings by leads converted to clients). "Active Clients" and "Group Members" reflect the current count. All of these update automatically — there is nothing to enter manually.

features.title: Manual tracking ("Other")
features.body: When you choose the "Other — Manual Updates" metric, you also choose how to track it: "Manual Entry" or "Daily Check-In Question". A manual goal card has an "Enter" button to log progress, and a "History" button with the entry count that opens all entries to view or delete.

features.title: Linking to a daily check-in question
features.body: For a manual goal you can choose "Daily Check-In Question": link an existing question, or write a new one — including the wording, answer type ("Scale 1–10" or "Yes / No"), icon, and when it appears. Numeric answers accumulate toward the goal: a score of 7 on the scale adds 7, and a "Yes" answer adds 1.

features.title: Cap for a yes/no question goal
features.body: When the daily check-in question is "Yes / No" type, the system calculates how many times the question will appear in the period and does not let you set a target higher than that. A message shows how many times the question will appear, and that you can aim for fewer but not more. Scale questions have no such cap.

features.title: Entering progress
features.body: The "Enter Progress" window asks for a numeric value, a date (defaults to today, future dates are not allowed), and an optional note. Entries accumulate toward the goal's result for that period.

features.title: Each goal's card
features.body: Each card shows the goal's name, category, and time frame, the overall achievement percentage (with "+" when it exceeds 100%), and two bars — "of Goal" (how much has been achieved) and "of Pace" (how on-pace you are relative to time elapsed). Next to them are the value versus the target and an importance rating in stars.

features.title: Editing and deleting
features.body: Each card has an edit button (pencil) to change the name, time frame, target, importance, project and group assignment, and tracking method (you can also swap the linked daily question), and a delete button (trash). Deleting a goal asks for confirmation and notes that you can restore it from Trash within 30 days.

tips: Give your goal a clear number — "20 active clients" works much better than "grow my practice".

The two bars mean different things: "of Goal" shows how much has been achieved in total, and "of Pace" shows whether you are on track relative to how much time has already passed in the period. If "of Pace" is below 100%, you are behind — even if "of Goal" is moving forward.
For a yes/no question goal you can aim for fewer days than the question is asked (for example, target 3 per week even if the question appears 5 times), but not for more.
Even for a goal linked to a daily question, the "Enter" button is still there — a manual entry counts on top of question answers, not instead of them.
Importance (1–5) determines how much weight the goal carries in the overall score in Overview — a more important goal pulls the score more strongly.
If you accidentally deleted a goal or an entry, the Trash has a 30-day window for recovery, and deleting an entry also shows an immediate Undo option.

faq.q: Where do I manage goal categories?
faq.a: There is no separate category management here. The category is set by the metric you choose when creating the goal, and it is created automatically — all goals are grouped by it. Automatic metrics are tracked on their own, and every manual goal falls under the "Other" category.

faq.q: Why is my goal's progress not updating?
faq.a: It depends on the metric: "Revenue" only sums confirmed income transactions in the period, "Leads" are counted by the lead's inquiry date, "Closings" only count leads converted to clients, and "Active Clients" only counts clients with an active status. For a manual goal you need to log values via "Enter", or answer the linked daily check-in question.

faq.q: What is the difference between "of Goal" and "of Pace" on the card?
faq.a: "of Goal" is the achievement percentage against the full target. "of Pace" compares your progress to the expected pace based on how much time has already passed in the period — if you are halfway through the month and have reached 50% of your target, "of Pace" shows 100%. For metrics that are a current count (active clients, group members) and for "By Date" goals with a target of 1, there is no separate pace calculation, and both bars show the same value.

faq.q: I linked a daily question to my goal — how does it accumulate?
faq.a: Every numeric answer in the period is added to the result: for a 1–10 scale question the value itself accumulates (answer 7 = 7), and for a yes/no question each "Yes" adds 1. Days you did not answer add nothing.

faq.q: I accidentally deleted a goal — can I get it back?
faq.a: Yes. Deleting a goal sends it to Trash, and you can restore it within 30 days. Deleting a manual entry can also be undone — an Undo option appears immediately after deletion.

faq.q: Can I link a goal to a project or group?
faq.a: Yes. The goal window has a "Project (optional)" selector, and if that project has groups a "Group (optional)" selector appears too. For a "Group Members" goal, the assignment also narrows the count to that specific group or project.

insights.title: Daily Check-In
insights.intro: This is your daily personal check-in screen. Answer each question on its card, and you get a reflection, averages, a trend chart, and six months of history for each question.

features.title: Daily reflection
features.body: The "Daily Reflection" card at the top of the screen shows up to three sentences written automatically from your answers — a streak of days you have answered, a weekly high or low for a specific question, a rise or drop compared to last week, or an encouraging stability note when there is no major change. It relies only on active questions and updates on its own.

features.title: A card for each question
features.body: Every question you have set up appears as its own card with its icon and wording. Disabled questions also appear, in a muted style, so you can turn them on or off right here.

features.title: Daily answer
features.body: For a 1–10 scale question, move the slider and click the checkmark to save. For a "Yes / No" question, click Yes or No. You can only answer a question that is active, scheduled for today, and that you have not yet answered today.

features.title: Skipping a question
features.body: The "Skip" button leaves the question unanswered for today. No answer is recorded, so your streak, averages, and trends are not affected. The skip resets automatically the next day.

features.title: Restoring skipped questions
features.body: If you skipped questions you can still answer today, a button appears below the cards: "Answer N skipped questions" (or "Answer 1 skipped question" when there is only one), which brings all of them back to answer.

features.title: Toggle for each question
features.body: Each card has a toggle that enables or disables the question directly from this screen. A disabled question stays on the screen but cannot be answered and does not count toward the reflection or your streak.

features.title: Averages and change
features.body: Each card shows a "7-day average", with a tag next to it showing the change compared to the seven days before that, and also a "30-day average". Averages do not count days without an answer.

features.title: Trend chart
