features.body: Under "Last 30 days" a line chart appears showing your answers over the past month. A day without an answer is drawn as a gap and is not connected by a line — you need at least two data points for the chart to appear.

features.title: Six-month heat map
features.body: "Last 6 months" shows a grid of 26 weeks, one cell per day. The higher the answer, the darker and fuller the cell. For yes/no questions the cell is full for "Yes" and light for "No". Hovering over a cell shows the date and value.

features.title: History
features.body: At the bottom of the screen you can expand "History" to see the last 30 answers, newest first, with the icon, question wording, date, and value. If you opened it, it stays open on your next visits. Each answer has a delete button, for one logged on the wrong day — it is kept in the trash for 30 days.

features.title: Managing questions in Settings
features.body: Add, delete, and schedule questions in Settings > Daily questions. There you can add a question from a ready-made template or write your own (text, answer type, and icon), and set whether it appears "Every day", on "Specific days", or "Every X days".

tips: Answer every day — even one question keeps your streak alive. The charts and reflection start getting interesting after about three weeks of data.
If a question is not relevant today, it is better to click "Skip" than to give an inaccurate answer. Skipping does not affect your averages or trends.
Weekly highs and lows appear in the reflection only for 1–10 scale questions, and only when there are enough answers in that week. Yes/no questions are not included in that calculation.
A question you disabled stays on the screen in a muted style with all its history — you can re-enable it at any time using the toggle on the card.
To change which days a question appears, open the scheduling row in Settings > Daily questions and choose "Specific days" or "Every X days".

faq.q: Can I write a free-text answer?
faq.a: Not on this screen. Answers are only given with a 1–10 slider or yes/no buttons, depending on the answer type you set for the question in Settings.

faq.q: I already answered today — how do I change my answer?
faq.a: Once you answer, the card shows a "Today · N" tag and the answer row disappears, so you cannot change today's answer from this screen.

faq.q: The questions are not showing up to answer?
faq.a: The answer row only appears when the question is active (toggle is on), today is a day it is scheduled to appear, and you have not already answered it today. If you skipped it, it will come back via the "Answer skipped questions" button.

faq.q: Where do I add or delete questions?
faq.a: In Settings > Daily questions. On the Daily Check-In screen you can only enable, disable, and answer — not add or delete. Skipping a question for today moved to the "How are you today" widget on the Home screen.

faq.q: Are there correlations between metrics here?
faq.a: No. Cross-metric relationships and combined charts are in the Overview screen. Here each question stands on its own, with its own average, trend, and heat map.

faq.q: What do the colors in the heat map mean?
faq.a: There is no green or red here. Cell intensity shows how high the value is: a higher value looks fuller and darker, a lower value looks lighter, and a day with no answer stays empty.

moon.title: Overview
moon.intro: A single high-level view of your entire practice: one weighted score, a breakdown by goal category, a trend over time, and connections between different areas. Everything is based on the goals you've set.

features.title: The Main Score (On Pace)
features.body: At the center of the screen is a ring with a large percentage and the label "On Pace" below it. This shows how much progress you've made relative to what's expected so far within each goal's period. Below that you'll see "X% of target" — your achievement against the full target. The score is weighted by goal importance, and each goal is capped at 100 before weighting.

features.title: Reflection Sentence
features.body: Below the ring is a short sentence that changes based on your score — for example, "You're on a great track this month" for a high score, or "Let's build some momentum — one small step forward" for a low score. This isn't a judgment of good or bad; it's just a hint about your current pace.

features.title: Breakdown by Category
features.body: Each goal category that has goals gets a card with two bars side by side: "On Pace" (how you're doing relative to the expected pace) and "Of Target" (percentage of the full target). This lets you see which areas are pulling your score up and which are pulling it down. Values above 100% are shown as a number, but the bar itself stops at 100%.

features.title: Trend Over Time
features.body: A line graph of your score over the last 30 days, with three metrics alongside it: "Average", "Peak", and "Today". The line is recalculated from your current data day by day, and any day that has a real saved snapshot overrides the calculation for that day — true history where it was recorded, an estimate elsewhere. Today itself is always live, so the end of the line, the "Today" figure and the ring above it all show the same number.

features.title: What moves together
features.body: This section lives under "Go deeper" at the bottom of the screen — tap it to open. A graph that displays several metrics together on the same axis. Use the buttons to choose what to show: revenue, leads, sessions, score, or daily check-in. By default, revenue and score are shown. Each line is scaled to its own range (0–100), so you can compare the shape of the trend even across things measured differently (₪, counts, 1–10). If there isn't enough data, you'll see "Not enough data for the graph yet".

features.title: Selecting a Daily Check-In in the Graph
features.body: The "Daily Check-In" button is only active if you have active daily check-in questions set up. When you select it, a list opens to choose which question to display on the graph. Days you didn't answer appear as a gap in the line (not as zero), so the data isn't misleading.

features.title: Links to Explore
features.body: This section lives under "Go deeper" at the bottom of the screen — tap it to open. The system automatically checks whether there's a connection between numerical daily check-in questions (scale 1–10) — primarily between two daily questions, and in principle also against revenue, leads, and sessions. Most of the time you'll see "No significant connection in the data right now", and that's completely fine. When a stable pattern appears, it's shown as a card describing that the metrics "tend to move together" or "move inversely", with a strength label (strong, moderate, or subtle), a point count, and a small scatter plot.

features.title: Navigating to Reports and Goals
features.body: The "Reports" button at the top of the screen takes you to the Reports screen for deeper analysis. At the bottom of the screen, "Edit your goals →" takes you to the Goals screen — that's where you change the data that feeds into this entire score.

tips: This entire screen is based on your goals — without at least one goal defined, you'll only see an empty message. Go to the Goals screen, set a goal, and come back.

The difference between "On Pace" and "Of Target" matters: "Of Target" tells you how much of the full goal has been achieved, while "On Pace" tells you whether you're moving at the right speed for the time that's passed in the period. You can be 40% of your target but 100% on pace if it's still early in the month.
Watch the line in "Trend Over Time" over weeks, not day by day — a single point tells you less than a trend.

In the "What moves together" graph, each line is scaled to its own range, so you're comparing the shape of the trend, not the absolute values. The actual values appear in the graph legend (window sum for revenue, leads, and sessions; the last answered value for score and daily check-in).
A connection you see here — visual or statistical — is not cause and effect. The cards are intentionally phrased as "tend to move together", not "X causes Y".

faq.q: The screen is empty and says there are no goals — why?
faq.a: The entire score is calculated from your goals. Without at least one goal, there's nothing to calculate, which is why you see "No goals yet". Go to the Goals screen, set a goal, and come back.

faq.q: What's the difference between the large percentage (On Pace) and the "X% of target" below it?
faq.a: The large percentage is "On Pace" — how much progress you've made relative to what's expected so far in the period. "X% of target" is your achievement against the full target. At the start of a month, you can be high on pace but still low against the full target.

faq.q: Do the bars in each category compare this week to last week?
faq.a: No. The two bars in each category are "On Pace" and "Of Target" for that category — there's no week-over-week comparison on this screen. Period comparisons are available in the Reports screen.

faq.q: Why does it say "No significant connection in the data right now" in Links to Explore?
faq.a: That's the normal, expected result. The system only shows a connection if it's stable and statistically reliable enough (including checking whether the connection is real, comparing the two halves of the period, and correcting for multiple comparisons). In a 120-day window, what typically clears the bar is a connection between two numerical daily check-in questions, and it usually takes a few weeks of answers before anything appears.

faq.q: Why is the "Daily Check-In" button in the graph disabled?
faq.a: The button only becomes active if you have active daily check-in questions. Enable or create a question in Settings → Daily questions, and then you'll be able to select it and see it on the graph.

faq.q: The score isn't changing — why?
faq.a: The score updates when the data feeding your goals changes: confirmed income transactions (not ones awaiting approval or marked "Didn't happen"), daily check-in answers, number of active clients, leads and lead conversions, group member counts, and manual entries you've logged in goals. Update those and the score will move.

reports.title: Reports
reports.intro: The Reports screen shows you 13 numbers that summarize your practice month by month — leads, clients, sessions, finances, and tasks. You can view a single month in list mode, or compare multiple months side by side in table mode. And you can click any number to see exactly which records make it up.

features.title: Two Views — List and Table
features.body: At the top is a toggle between "List" and "Table". "List" shows one month at a time, with numbers organized by topic. "Table" spreads them all out side by side, one column per month. Your choice is saved and restored next time.

features.title: 12-Month Bar (List View)
features.body: In list view there's a bar showing the last 12 months. Click a month to see all its numbers. The current month is selected by default.

features.title: Month Range in Table View
features.body: In table view you choose how many months back to show — 3, 6, or 12. There's a column for each month (the current month is highlighted) and a "Summary" column at the end. Your selection is saved automatically.

features.title: The Summary Column
features.body: The "Summary" column in the table sums up the entire range, but not everything works the same way. Things that flow over time (leads, sessions, revenue) are simply added up. End-of-month snapshots (active clients at end, open tasks at end) are averaged. And percentages (conversion rate, mid-journey drop-offs) are recalculated across the full range.

features.title: The 13 Numbers by Group
features.body: The numbers are organized into five groups: Leads (new leads, leads closed, converted to clients, conversion rate), Clients (new clients, active clients at end, mid-journey drop-offs), Sessions (sessions held), Finances (revenue, expenses, net), and Tasks (tasks completed, open tasks at end).

features.title: Drilling Down to Records
features.body: Click a number in list view, or a non-empty cell in table view, and a panel opens showing you the actual records behind it — leads, clients, sessions, transactions, or tasks — along with their total count.

features.title: Deleted records still count
features.body: Deleting tidies your screens — it does not undo what happened. A month that has passed keeps showing the inquiries it received, the sessions that took place and the tasks you finished, after you delete them and after they are permanently removed from the server: the numbers were counted the moment the things happened. In the drill-down a recently deleted record is marked "in the trash"; one that has already been permanently deleted is not listed at all, and instead you see how many records can no longer be shown. Two exceptions: for money, a deleted transaction leaves income, expense and net — a transaction is usually deleted because it was wrong, not for tidiness. And for the "at the end" numbers, a client or task deleted during the month is not counted at its end, because it was no longer there.

features.title: Navigating from the Drill-Down to the Screen
features.body: Every row in the drill-down window is a link. Tapping it takes you to the matching screen — leads, clients, calendar, money or tasks. A row marked "in the trash" leads to the trash, since the record is no longer on the screen it was deleted from. Note: the link takes you to the screen, not always to the specific record.

features.title: Choosing Numbers and Order
features.body: The gear button "Customize view" opens a panel where you toggle which numbers to show (a switch for each) and change the order with the arrows beside each row. With a mouse you can also drag the handle. Your choices and order apply to both views.

features.title: Restoring Defaults
features.body: In the customization panel there's a "Default" button that restores all 13 numbers in their original order with one click.

features.title: Explanations for the Numbers
features.body: Next to "Leads closed" there's a "?" icon. Hover over it or tap it to see a short explanation: "Leads closed" counts everyone who exited the process — whether converted to a client or marked as not relevant. "Converted to clients" counts only those who actually became clients.

features.title: Month with No Data
features.body: If the month you selected has no data, you'll see "No data for this month". If another month has activity, you'll be offered a button to jump to it ("Go to...") — the most recent month that has something.

features.title: Link to Overview
features.body: At the top there's a "Overview" link that takes you to the Overview screen for a broader picture of your activity.

tips: Income, expense and net count only transactions you have confirmed. An unconfirmed transaction will not appear in the report, and a deleted one leaves the figures too — money is the only thing that behaves this way.
The Summary column in the table isn't always a simple sum: the "at end" numbers are averages, and percentages are recalculated. So don't expect the summary to be exactly the sum of the columns.
A cell or number that equals 0 can't be clicked. You can only drill down into numbers that have something behind them.

Use the gear button to hide numbers you don't care about and keep the report focused. Hiding doesn't delete anything — it just removes it from view. And if you hide everything, the table will let you know there are no active numbers.
"Active clients at end" and "Open tasks at end" are snapshots of how things looked at the end of the month — not a count of everything that happened during it.
List view only shows the last 12 months. Want a different range? Switch to table view and choose 3, 6, or 12 months.

faq.q: Where do I choose a custom date range?
faq.a: There's no custom date range here. In list view you pick one month from the 12-month bar, and in table view you choose how many months back — 3, 6, or 12. This screen doesn't have a line graph or a revenue breakdown by category.

faq.q: The report shows 0 revenue even though I have transactions?
faq.a: Only confirmed transactions are counted, based on their date. Check that the transactions are confirmed and that their dates fall within the month you selected. If the number is still 0 — it might be hidden, so check the gear button to make sure it's toggled on.

faq.q: What's the difference between "Leads closed" and "Converted to clients"?
faq.a: "Leads closed" counts every lead that left the process — either converted or marked not relevant. "Converted" counts only those that actually became clients, so it is usually lower. Deleting a lead does not close it: a lead you deleted while it was still in process is not counted as closed.

faq.q: Why doesn't the summary in the table equal the sum of the columns?
faq.a: It depends on the number. Things that flow (leads, sessions, money) are truly summed. But "end of month" numbers are averaged, and conversion rate and drop-off rate are recalculated across the full range — because you can't simply add percentages.

faq.q: I changed which numbers are shown and their order — will it be saved?
faq.a: Yes. Your choices, order, view (list or table), and range are all saved automatically and restored next time, even from a different device. The "Default" button resets the selection and order back to the original.

faq.q: What happens when I click a number in the report?
faq.a: A panel opens showing you the actual records behind the number, along with their count. Clicking a row in the panel takes you to the relevant screen — Leads, Clients, Calendar, Finance, or Tasks.

faq.q: I deleted a record and the number did not drop — why?
faq.a: That is how it is meant to work. The report says what happened in the month, and deleting something later does not undo it — otherwise every tidy-up of your clients or tasks screen would shrink closed months. That holds even after the record is permanently removed from the server, because the number was counted when it happened and does not depend on the record. In the drill-down a recently deleted record shows as "in the trash", and if records have already been permanently deleted you are told how many cannot be shown. The exception: deleted transactions do leave the money figures.

connections.title: Connections
connections.intro: The Connections screen is where you manage Simplicity's integrations with external services — Google Calendar and invoicing (Green Invoice or SUMIT). Each has its own page where you can connect, disconnect, and manage the integration.

features.title: The Connections List
features.body: The screen shows two rows: Google Calendar and Invoicing. Each row shows its current status — the calendar shows "Connected" or "Not connected", and invoicing shows "Not connected", "Connected" with the provider name, or "Reconnection required". Click a row to enter its management page. The connect and disconnect buttons are inside the page, so clicking a row won't accidentally disconnect anything.

features.title: WhatsApp and Claude
features.body: WhatsApp is now a live row — manual sending of messages to clients: a WhatsApp button appears on the client card, in the calendar, on lead follow-ups, and on receipts. Tapping it opens a ready-made message you can edit before sending, and inside the page you can set the default wording for each message type. Below it one row is marked "Coming soon" — Claude; its toggle is off and can't be clicked.

features.title: Connecting Google Calendar
features.body: On the Google Calendar page, choose how far back to start syncing ("Sync from date"). The default is one year back, and you can't go further than that. Click "Connect Google Calendar", and Google's permissions screen will open. Once you approve, events will start coming into the app automatically.

features.title: Syncing and Disconnecting the Calendar
features.body: When the calendar is connected, you can see when it was last synced. The "Sync now" button pulls in events again and tells you how many were added and how many were removed. The "Disconnect" button requires a second click to confirm ("Are you sure? Disconnect").

features.title: Synced Events and How They're Identified
features.body: Under "Synced events" you can see your events, grouped by clients, projects, leads, groups, and "Unidentified". Each event is marked "Identified" or "Unidentified" based on its association, with the date, time, and session length shown alongside.

features.title: Manually Associating an Event
features.body: For any event you can click "+ Associate with…", choose what to link it to (client, project, lead, or group), and then select the specific record from the list. You can also remove an existing association with the X on its tag. Associations you set manually are saved and won't be overwritten by future syncs.

features.title: Connecting Invoicing (Green Invoice / SUMIT)
features.body: On the Invoicing page, choose a provider — "Green Invoice" or "SUMIT" — and paste in your credentials. For Green Invoice: API Key and Secret (the key and secret from your service account). For SUMIT: Company ID and API Key. The "How do I get these?" button walks you through exactly where to find them in each service.

features.title: Testing, Disconnecting, and Reconnecting
features.body: After connecting, the status shows "Connected" with the provider name. "Test connection" verifies with the service that your credentials are still valid, and "Disconnect" requires a second click. If the key was revoked or replaced, you'll see "Reconnection required" with a "Reconnect" button to enter new credentials.

features.title: Auto-Importing Revenue
features.body: When invoicing is connected, you can turn on the "Auto-import revenue?" checkbox. When it's on, the system detects invoices you've issued in your invoicing software and asks whether to record them as revenue here too. It won't record anything without your confirmation.

features.title: Invoices You Issued in Your Invoicing Service
features.body: Below the invoicing card there's an "Invoices you issued in your invoicing service" list — invoices you've issued in the external service that are waiting for your approval. Each row shows the document type and number, amount, client name, a "View" link to the document (if available), and an import button ("Import as income") or a reject button. Importing opens a confirmation dialog showing exactly what will be recorded. If it looks like a duplicate of an existing transaction, that same dialog is worded as a stronger warning.

tips: For Google Calendar, if you choose an earlier start date before connecting, you'll pull in a longer history of events. After connecting, you can't extend the range further back without disconnecting and reconnecting (and even then, no more than one year back).
Events the system didn't recognize ("Unidentified") are worth associating manually — with a client, project, lead, or group. The association is saved and won't be overwritten by future syncs.
Not sure if your invoicing credentials are still valid? Click "Test connection" on the Invoicing page. It checks with the service without disconnecting anything.
The Secret for Green Invoice is only shown once, when you create the key. Copy it right away, before you close the window.

If you've already recorded revenue manually and it also appears under "Invoices you issued in your invoicing service" with a "Possibly a duplicate" label — reject the import so it doesn't get recorded twice.
For SUMIT you need the private API key, not the public one. Otherwise the connection will fail.

faq.q: I connected Google Calendar but the events aren't showing up?
faq.a: Go to the Google Calendar page and click "Sync now". If events still don't appear, they may be outside the date range you chose when connecting — disconnect and reconnect with an earlier start date.

faq.q: Can I connect both Green Invoice and SUMIT at the same time?
faq.a: No. The Invoicing page supports one active provider at a time, and connecting a different provider replaces the previous one. Choose the service you work with.

faq.q: Can I issue an invoice to a client from this screen?
faq.a: Not directly. This screen is only for connecting the service. To issue an invoice or receipt, go to a revenue transaction in the Finance screen — the connection is what enables that option there.

faq.q: What do I do when it says "Reconnection required"?
faq.a: It means the service rejected the credentials you saved — they were probably revoked or replaced. Click "Reconnect", enter new credentials, and click connect.

faq.q: The "Auto-import revenue?" checkbox — does it record revenue without asking me?
faq.a: No. When it's on, it detects invoices you've issued in your invoicing software and adds them to the "Invoices you issued in your invoicing service" list. But they're only recorded as revenue after you confirm each one yourself.

faq.q: Where are the credentials I entered stored?
faq.a: Your credentials are stored on our servers and are linked only to your account. The browser doesn't read them back, and there's no way to view them again from the screen — not even for you.

settings.title: Settings
settings.intro: Settings is where you make the app yours. It has four areas — Personal, Look and display, My work, and My account — with a search field on top, for when typing what you want beats guessing where it lives.

features.title: Search — the short way
features.body: A search field sits at the top. Type a word — a synonym works too, like "shekel", "font", "backup" or "calendar" — and the screen narrows to the matching setting, already open and ready to change. The ✕ clears the search and brings every area back.

features.title: How the screen is built — four areas
features.body: Personal · Look and display · My work · My account. Each opens on a tap and holds sections, and all start closed. An area with a single section inside — "Personal" — opens straight to its content, with no second door.

features.title: Personal — your name, form of address and profession
features.body: Fill in your full name, choose a form of address (feminine, masculine or neutral), and pick a profession from the buttons. Choosing "Other" opens a free-text field for what you actually do. The form of address changes the wording across the whole app.

features.title: Saved automatically, and confirmed
features.body: There is no save button. The name and the free-text field save the moment you leave them — even if you closed the area first. Every change raises a short "Setting saved" note, and if a save fails (a dropped connection, usually) a red message appears at the top instead of the value quietly reverting.

features.title: Look and display — Appearance
features.body: Everything about how the app looks lives here: language, light/dark, background, text size, and under "Card look" — style (Glass or Solid), letter thickness (Regular or Thick) and spacing between items (Tight, Regular or Roomy). The Hebrew-calendar switches sit at the bottom.

features.title: A sample card that changes with you
features.body: Above the card controls sits a real sample card that changes in real time with every choice. That way you can see what "Glass" or "Roomy" does without leaving the screen — the result of those choices normally lives on other screens.

features.title: Home screen — what appears and in what order
features.body: A list of every card on the home screen, with a switch to show or hide it and arrows to reorder. You can also arrange and hide them on the home screen itself — press and hold a card. The arrows stay here for anyone not working with a mouse or touch.

features.title: Currency, date and time
features.body: Choose a currency, a date format, a clock and the day your week starts on. The date and time options show today and now in each format — so you see the result and pick what reads well, instead of decoding an abbreviation.

features.title: My work — meeting types and prices
features.body: Your price list: a name for each meeting type and a default price. A price set on a type applies automatically to the clients linked to it — unless they have a manual price. Name and price are editable straight in the row.

features.title: Daily questions and the reminder
features.body: You start with no questions and add them through "Add question" — a ready template or your own, with an answer type (a 1–10 scale or yes/no) and an icon. Tapping the schedule label opens "Every day" / "Certain days" / "Every X days". At the bottom you can turn on a daily reminder and pick a time; if you have not answered by then, a gentle nudge appears on the "How are you today" card.

features.title: Statuses, labels and sources — on their own screens
features.body: Client sub-statuses, and lead labels and sources, are managed on the screens that use them — not here. Settings has rows that lead there: "Client sub-statuses" opens the clients screen (where a "Sub-statuses" button opens the editor — add, rename, and delete with a move for the clients on it), and "Lead labels and sources" opens the leads screen.

features.title: My account — Data
features.body: The top of the section shows how many of everything you have. "Export data" opens one window: an Excel file with a sheet per type, or a separate CSV export of transactions / clients / projects. "Import from a file" reads CSV, TSV and Excel, recognises columns on its own and lets you correct them before anything is written. "Start the intro over" is here too.

features.title: Exporting sensitive data (optional)
features.body: The export window has checkboxes for sensitive data — sessions, goals, daily answers and reflections. They are off by default and reset every time the window opens. Ticking one adds sheets to the file, and the data leaves as plain text — so keep the file somewhere safe.

features.title: Reset and delete — a section of its own
features.body: The two actions that cannot be undone sit in their own section, not at the bottom of the export scroll. "Erase all data and start over" clears the account's contents and restarts the intro. "Delete the account permanently" removes the whole account including your login — with a 30-day grace period to change your mind. Both ask again after you press.

features.title: About, and the ways out
features.body: "About" holds the version, the principles and the links to the Privacy Policy, Terms of Use and Data Processing Agreement. The same area has rows leading to "Connections" (Google Calendar, invoices, WhatsApp) and to "Trash". The full guide and the FAQ moved to a help screen of their own — reach it from the menu ("Help and guide") or from the ? button at the top of any screen.

tips: Not sure where something lives? Don't guess — type the word into the search field at the top. Even "shekel" or "font" will get you there.
Language is under "Look and display → Appearance", together with light/dark and text size — not under "Personal".
Everything saves itself. The "Setting saved" note is the confirmation; if something fails you get a red message, not silence.
Want to see what "Glass" or "Roomy" does? The sample card above the controls changes with you in real time.
Client sub-statuses and lead labels are edited on their own screens. The rows in Settings are the shortcut there.

faq.q: Where do I change the language?
faq.a: Settings → Look and display → Appearance. It sits there with light/dark, the background and text size, and switches immediately.

faq.q: Where do I add or delete a client sub-status?
faq.a: On the clients screen — the "Sub-statuses" button in the toolbar. You can add, rename (tap the name) and delete; deleting one that has clients on it asks where to move them. Settings has a row that leads there.

faq.q: Where are the lead labels and sources?
faq.a: On the leads screen — the "Statuses" tab manages the labels (stages in "In process", reasons in "Not relevant") and the "Sources" button manages where enquiries come from. Settings has a row that leads there.

faq.q: Where are the full guide and the FAQ?
faq.a: On a help screen of their own: menu ("More") → "Help and guide". You can also get there from the ? button at the top of any screen, via "The full guide to every screen".

faq.q: I changed a setting and I'm not sure it saved
faq.a: Every change raises a short "Setting saved" note. If a red message appeared at the top, the save failed — usually a dropped connection — and it is worth trying again.

faq.q: Why is "Delete account" no longer under "Data"?
faq.a: It got its own section, "Reset and delete", so it would not share a scroll with export and import. The actions themselves did not change, and neither did the double confirmation.

trash.title: Trash
trash.intro: Here you can view and restore items you've deleted — clients, transactions, sessions, tasks, leads, goals and more — for 30 days from the moment you deleted them.

features.title: Every deletion here is still reversible
features.body: Almost every deletion in the app doesn't remove the item immediately — it moves here, to the Trash. At the top you can see how many items are here ("N items"), alongside the reminder "Kept for 30 days" and the message "Every deletion here is still reversible."

features.title: Items are organized by type
features.body: Deleted items are grouped by type, and each group shows an icon, name and item count. Types include: clients, projects, groups, tasks, leads, lead sources, lead labels, transactions, expense categories, recurring templates, sessions, reminders, goals, goal metrics, goal entries, daily questions and daily answers.

features.title: Restoring an item
features.body: Every item has a "Restore" button. Clicking it returns the item to the screen it was deleted from, with all its data. During the operation the button shows "Restoring…". You don't need to select an item first — the button acts directly on that row.

features.title: When each item was deleted
features.body: Below each item's name it shows "Deleted" and how long ago that happened (e.g. "Deleted 3 days ago"). This makes it easy to know how much time is left before it disappears from the Trash.

features.title: Kept for 30 days, then deleted
features.body: The Trash shows only items deleted in the last 30 days, and you can restore them from there. After 30 days a nightly sweep removes them from the server for good — they do not just drop off the list, they are really gone, and nothing can bring them back. So if there is something you might want, restore it in time. Reports are unaffected: the numbers were counted when the things happened, and they stay after the records themselves are deleted.

features.title: Empty trash
features.body: When there's nothing to restore, you'll see a message that "The trash is empty", with a note that anything you delete in the future will wait here for 30 days. There's nothing to do here — it simply means nothing has been deleted recently.

tips: Restoring returns the item exactly to the place it was deleted from (clients, transactions, goals, etc.) with all its data. No need to re-enter anything.

If you just deleted something by mistake, it's faster to click "Undo" on the brief notification that pops up after the deletion (for about 6 seconds). The Trash is your safety net for when that notification is already gone.
If you might want an item back, restore it within 30 days of deleting it. After that it is permanently removed from the server and cannot be recovered by any means.
Before deleting your account or doing a major cleanup, back up your data via Settings → Data → Export Data.

faq.q: How do I delete an item from the Trash for good?
faq.a: There is no permanent-delete button here, and no need for one — the only action is "Restore". Items are removed on their own: a nightly sweep deletes everything that was deleted more than 30 days ago. If you want to clear everything at once instead of waiting, that is in Settings → Reset and delete.

faq.q: I can't find an item I deleted?
faq.a: More than 30 days may have passed since the deletion, in which case it's no longer shown in the Trash. Another possibility: the item is restored together with its parent (like group members), or one of the groups failed to load — in which case an error message appears at the top.

faq.q: What happens when an item is restored?
faq.a: It returns immediately to the screen it was deleted from, with all its data, and disappears from the Trash. The update is instant visually, and syncs to the server in the background. If the server returns an error, the Trash reloads so what you see stays accurate.

faq.q: Does everything deleted in the app end up here?
faq.a: Almost every soft deletion lands in the Trash — clients, transactions, sessions, tasks, leads, goals and more. Some related items (like group members) are restored through their parent item, so they don't appear here separately.

faq.q: There's an error message at the top — what does that mean?
faq.a: It means one of the item groups failed to load. The other groups still display — one failed load doesn't empty the whole Trash. Try refreshing the page, and if the error persists, contact support.

admin.title: Admin Console
admin.intro: Management tools for the system owner: users, feedback and analytics.

features.title: User management
features.body: View all registered users, grant admin permissions, and delete accounts.

features.title: Feedback
features.body: All feedback submitted via the "Talk to us" button — read and respond.

features.title: Analytics
features.body: Usage data: number of active users, popular screens, and more.

items.q: I forgot my password — how do I reset it?
items.a: On the login screen, click "Forgot password?". Enter your email address and click "Send link". If the address is registered with us, we'll send a link to it. The link takes you to the "Choose a new password" screen, where you pick a new password (at least 6 characters) and confirm it.

items.q: How do I change my password when I'm already logged in?
items.a: Use the same "Choose a new password" screen. You can reach it via "Forgot password?" on the login screen, or via the reset link sent to your email.

items.q: How do I change my email address?
items.a: Currently, changing your account email address is only possible by contacting support.

items.q: I signed in with Google — do I need a password too?
items.a: No. With Google you don't need a password. Just click "Sign in with Google" each time.

items.q: Do I need to agree to anything when signing up?
items.a: Yes. When signing up (both with email and with Google) you check two boxes: one to accept the Privacy Policy and Data Processing Agreement, and one to accept the Terms of Use. There's also an optional box for marketing emails — it's not required and you can uncheck it at any time.

items.q: Who can see my data?
items.a: Only you. Each account is completely separate, and only you can see your account's data. The connection to the server is secure. We do not sell your data or share it with anyone.

items.q: Are sensitive fields encrypted in the database?
items.a: Notes, session summaries and reflections are stored on our end as plain text. What protects them: only you access your account, and the connection is secure. If you used early beta versions, some fields may still be stored in encrypted form from the past — they are decrypted automatically for you.

items.q: What happens to my Green Invoice / SUMIT API keys?
items.a: Your connection credentials (the identifier and key) are stored on our server only. They are never shown in the browser — not even to you. The system uses them only when it issues an invoice or pulls income on your behalf.

items.q: How do I back up my data?
items.a: Settings → Data → Export Data. You can download all your data in a single Excel file (one sheet per type: transactions, clients, projects, leads, tasks, categories). You can also export clients, transactions or projects separately as CSV files.

items.q: Can I include sensitive data (sessions, goals, daily answers, reflections) in the export?
items.a: Yes. The export dialog has checkboxes for this, and they are off by default. They add extra sheets to the full Excel file. Sensitive data exports as plain text, so keep the file somewhere safe.

items.q: How do I import data from Excel / Google Sheets?
items.a: Settings → Data → Import from File (CSV / Excel). You can upload CSV, TSV and Excel files (xlsx/xls), including files with multiple sheets. The system auto-detects the columns, and you can manually correct the mapping before importing.

items.q: How do I delete my account?
items.a: Settings → My account → Reset and delete. This deletes the entire account, including your login, and requires two confirmations with typed input. After deletion there is a 30-day grace period — during that time you can change your mind and cancel.

items.q: How do I switch to dark mode?
items.a: Open the menu ("More" in the navigation) and click the "Dark mode" toggle (when it's on it's called "Light mode"). You can also go to Settings → Appearance → Light/Dark Mode.

items.q: How do I make the text larger?
items.a: Settings → Appearance → Text Size. There are three options: small, normal, large.

items.q: How do I set my preferred form of address (masculine/feminine/neutral)?
items.a: Settings → Profile → Form of Address. Your choice (neutral / feminine / masculine) changes the wording throughout the entire app.

items.q: Can I change the order of screens in the navigation?
items.a: The screen order in navigation is fixed for now. You can customize the Home screen: Settings → Look and display → Home screen. There you enable and disable widgets, change their order and choose a display style.

items.q: The app is frozen / not loading?
items.a: Refresh the page (F5 on desktop, or pull down on mobile). If it continues — log out and log back in.

items.q: Data I saved isn't showing up?
items.a: Refresh the page. If something is still missing, check that you have an internet connection. If it continues, contact us via "Talk to us" in the menu.

items.q: The + button isn't responding?
items.a: There's probably a dialog or drawer open in the background. Close any open dialogs and try again.

items.q: Which services can I connect?
items.a: Currently: Google Calendar (pulls events from your calendar and identifies sessions with clients), an invoicing service — Green Invoice or SUMIT (issues invoices and receipts and imports income), and WhatsApp (manual sending of messages to clients, with wording you can customise). Claude is marked "Coming soon" and is not yet active.

items.q: How do I get to the Connections screen?
items.a: Via the "Connections" tab in the navigation. The screen shows a list: Google Calendar, Invoicing, and "Coming soon" rows. Each active row opens to its own screen where you connect and manage it.

items.q: How do I connect Google Calendar?
items.a: Connections → Google Calendar. Choose which date to sync from, click "Connect Google Calendar", and approve the permissions in the Google dialog. After that you can sync any time by clicking "Sync Now", and assign events to a client, project, lead or group.

items.q: How do I connect an invoicing service?
items.a: Connections → Invoicing. Choose a provider (Green Invoice or SUMIT), paste your credentials from your account with that service, and click "Connect". The "How do I get these?" button has step-by-step instructions.

items.q: Can I connect both Green Invoice and SUMIT?
items.a: Only one invoicing service at a time. To switch providers, disconnect the current one and connect the new one.

items.q: My invoicing service credentials aren't being accepted?
items.a: Make sure you copied the identifier and key in full, without spaces, and that you're using the private API key (not the public one). After connecting, you can verify with the "Check Connection" button. If the connection suddenly stopped working ("Reconnection required"), the key was probably revoked or replaced — click "Reconnect" and enter it again.

items.q: What does "Auto-import income" mean?
items.a: When this is turned on, the system detects income you've recorded in your invoicing software and shows it to you for approval. Nothing is recorded in your account without your confirmation.

about.tagline: Business OS — at your own pace
about.description: Simplicity was built for therapists, coaches, facilitators, teachers, instructors and consultants in Israel. One place for your entire practice: clients, leads, sessions and calendar, finance, projects, tasks, goals and your own personal process. All in Hebrew, in your preferred form of address (masculine/feminine/neutral), and without the clutter.

principles.title: Privacy first
principles.body: Your data is yours alone. Only you access your account, and the connection to the server is secure. Your invoicing service credentials are stored on our server and are never shown in the browser — not even to you. We do not sell data or rank you.

principles.title: An interface that respects you
principles.body: No noise. No "Premium" pop-ups. No unnecessary alerts. Just what you need to run a practice — at your own pace.

principles.title: Made in Israel
principles.body: Built in Hebrew, with a form of address that fits you (masculine/feminine/neutral), for the community of therapists, coaches and consultants here.
